name: Foundational identities for the Gowers norm and the k-AP counting operator

insights: The parent OQ-03 defines gowersNorm and kAPCount constructively but proves NO algebraic properties of them — this child fills that gap with the foundational degenerate/normalization identities.

kAPCount on a constant tuple (c,…,c) equals c^k: the inner product is c^k and the normalized double average (N^-1)^2 * sum_{x,d} c^k = c^k cancels N^2 against the (N^-1)^2 prefactor. The all-ones case gives Λ_k(1,…,1)=1, the total normalized k-AP mass.
A single zero argument annihilates the whole count (Finset.prod_eq_zero on the j-th factor) — the multiplicative analogue of linearity in each slot.
gowersNorm of the zero function is 0: conjugateByWeight ω 0 = 0 in both branches (identity and conjugation), so every 2^s-fold hypercube product vanishes.
These constant/zero base cases are exactly the start of the multilinear expansion 1_A = δ·1 + (1_A − δ) that opens the generalized von Neumann argument.

Parent RothTheoremOQ03.lean has TOOLCHAIN DRIFT on the current Mathlib (Complex.abs removed; Fin.val rewrite patterns and a dangling /-- docstring no longer parse) — this child is therefore SELF-CONTAINED, re-declaring the operators with the modern norm ‖·‖ so it builds independently of the broken parent.
norm notation ‖ ... ‖ wrapping a ∑/∏ that extends to the right swallows the closing bar — wrap the inner expression in explicit parentheses ‖(...)‖ (the parent dodged this with Complex.abs (...)).

Multilinearity of Λ_k is proved slotwise via Function.update: the j-th factor factors out of the product (Finset.mul_prod_erase + Function.update_apply), then additivity/homogeneity descend to the pointwise product and close by ring after Pi.add_apply / Pi.smul_apply+smul_eq_mul.
These two identities (additivity + homogeneity in each slot) are exactly the linear step of the generalized von Neumann argument: they license splitting one Λ_k slot as 1_A = δ·1 + (1_A − δ).

kAPCount_update_split (von Neumann slot-split): for any scalar δ, Λ_k(update f j g) = δ·Λ_k(update f j 1) + Λ_k(update f j (g − δ·1)). Proof = kAPCount_update_add on g = δ·1 + (g−δ·1) followed by kAPCount_update_smul; the δ·1 + (g−δ·1) = g step closes by add_sub_cancel. This is literally the first density-decomposition step of the generalized von Neumann argument (take g=1_A, δ=|A|/N).

kAPCount_update_sub: subtractivity in a slot, derived from update_add + update_smul via g₁−g₂ = g₁ + (−1)•g₂ (neg_one_smul, sub_eq_add_neg, neg_one_mul). Completes the slotwise linear structure (add/sub/smul/zero).
kAPCount_update_zero (@[simp]): overwriting slot j with 0 gives Λ_k = 0 — one-liner off kAPCount_eq_zero_of_zero + Function.update_self; the additive unit of the slot module.
Toolchain: Function.update_self (NOT update_same) is the v4.26 name for update f j v j = v; add_sub_cancel proves a + (b − a) = b here (works for the module ZMod N → ℂ).

The full slot-telescoping Λ_k(g,…,g)=∑_{S⊆[k]}δ^{k−|S|}Λ_k(i↦if i∈S then b else 1) (b=g−δ·1) is obtained in ONE shot from Finset.prod_add on the inner product ∏ᵢ g(x+i·d)=∏ᵢ(b(x+i·d)+δ), rather than iterating kAPCount_update_split k times. S=∅ gives the δ^k major term (kAPCount_const_one).

Assembly: expand inner product on both sides to a canonical triple sum (N⁻¹)²∑ₓ∑_d∑_S, then reconcile via two Finset.sum_comm reorderings (∑_S∑ₓ∑_d → ∑ₓ∑_d∑_S). RHS if-slots collapse via Finset.prod_ite_mem + univ_inter; δ-power exponent k−|S| via Finset.card_sdiff_of_subset.

To peel the S=∅ major term off Finset.univ sum over subsets: rw [← Finset.add_sum_erase Finset.univ _ (Finset.mem_univ ∅)] turns ∑_{S:Finset (Fin k)} into F ∅ + ∑_{S∈univ.erase ∅}; then the empty-slot tuple (fun i => if i∈∅ then b else 1) equals the const-1 tuple by funext i y; simp, so kAPCount_const_one evaluates it to 1 and the term is δ^k.

Combinatorial bridge (kAPCount_indicator_eq_count): feeding the complex indicator 1_A into every slot turns the analytic operator into a genuine count — Λ_k(1_A,…,1_A) = (N⁻¹)²·#{(x,d) : ∀ i, x+i·d ∈ A}, i.e. (N⁻¹)² times the number of length-k progressions x,x+d,…,x+(k−1)d lying wholly inside A. This is the concrete meaning of 'normalized k-AP density of A' that Roth's theorem (k=3) forces positive for dense A.

Proof recipe for indicator→count: simp only [kAPCount, indicatorZMod]; congr 1 (strip (N⁻¹)² prefactor); collapse the double average ∑_x∑_d to a single pair sum via `rw [← Finset.sum_product', Finset.univ_product_univ]` (sum_product' matches ∑x∈s∑y∈t f x y, avoids the (x,y).1 reconstruction that breaks Fintype.sum_prod_type); then `simp [Finset.prod_boole, Finset.sum_boole]` finishes (∏ of 0/1 indicators = indicator of ∀-condition, ∑ of that = card of the filtered pair set).

GOTCHA: `rw [Finset.sum_boole]` (and `rw`-ing any if-then-1-else-0 identity) FAILS 'did not find pattern' when the ite's Decidable instance is a concrete `decidableDforallFinset` (produced by prod_boole's bounded ∀ i∈univ) — rw won't unify the instance arg. Use `simp [Finset.sum_boole]` instead: simp is instance-robust AND simultaneously normalizes `∀ i ∈ univ` → `∀ i` so the counted filter predicate matches a plain-`∀ i` statement. Likewise hand-writing `if (∀ i ∈ univ, …) then 1 else 0` in a `have` fixes a DIFFERENT instance than prod_boole → later rw/exact mismatches; never restate the ite, let simp/library lemmas carry the instance.

Nondegenerate positivity ≠ nonemptiness: the total k-AP count vanishes iff A=∅ (kAPCount_count_eq_zero_iff), but the nondegenerate (d≠0) count already vanishes on the nonempty singleton {a} for k≥2 (kAPCount_nondeg_singleton, via i=1 term forcing d=0). This failure of nonempty⟹nondegenerate-progression is exactly why Roth is a genuine theorem, not the trivial diagonal count; the nondegenerate mass appears only once A is large enough.

SYMMETRY (researcher-5, 2026-07-11): the k-AP counting operator commutes with complex conjugation: starRingEnd ℂ (kAPCount k f) = kAPCount k (conj∘f) — proof is pure ring-hom distribution (map_mul/map_pow/map_inv₀/map_natCast on the (N⁻¹)² prefactor, then map_sum/map_sum/map_prod through the double average and the length-k product). Corollary: real-valued inputs (indicatorZMod, taking values 0/1) give a self-conjugate, i.e. real, count — consistent with kAPCount_indicator_eq_count = (N⁻¹)²·(count:ℕ). Adds the conjugation half of the analytic API needed for the Gowers-norm/von-Neumann program.

Session 2026-07-12 (researcher-8): completed the affine-invariance suite of the combinatorial k-AP count. The file had translation (kAPCount_count_translate) and negation/reflection (kAPCount_count_neg) invariance; added dilation invariance by a unit c∈(ℤ/N)ˣ — kAPCount_count_dilate + kAPCount_nondeg_dilate + analytic kAPCount_indicator_dilate. The map (x,d)↦(c·x,c·d) is a pair bijection (c a unit), subsuming negation (c=−1). Now the full affine group AGL(1,ℤ/N)=translations⋊dilations acts invariantly on the count. 0-axiom, docker-verified [7743]. Proofs mirror the negation lemmas with −1 generalized to a unit via Units.mul_inv/inv_mul cancellation; GOTCHA congrArg(fun z=>..)h leaves an un-beta-reduced lambda so rw[←mul_assoc] fails — use have h2:..:=by rw[h] instead.

Session 2026-07-12 (researcher-2): added the first ANALYTIC estimate on Λ_k (all prior lemmas were algebraic identities / symmetries / affine invariances). kAPCount_norm_le: ‖Λ_k(f)‖ ≤ ∏ᵢ Mᵢ when ‖f i x‖ ≤ M i — triangle inequality (norm_sum_le twice, norm_prod, Finset.prod_le_prod) passes the norm through the E_{x,d} average and the length-k product; the N² average terms cancel the (N⁻¹)² prefactor (ZMod.card + inv_mul_cancel_left₀). This is the trivial L^∞ generalized von Neumann bound.

kAPCount_diag_sub_major_norm_le (sup-norm generalized von Neumann bound): with b = g − δ·1 the balanced part, ‖δ‖≤1, ‖b‖_∞≤β≤1 ⟹ ‖Λ_k(g,…,g) − δ^k‖ ≤ 2^k·β. Proof: triangle on the 2^k−1 remainder terms of kAPCount_diag_eq_major_add_remainder; each term ‖δ^{k−|S|}·Λ_k(slot_S)‖ ≤ 1·β since ‖δ‖^{k−|S|}≤1 (pow_le_one₀) and ‖Λ_k(slot_S)‖ ≤ ∏(if i∈S then β else 1) ≤ β (prod_ite_le_self: β^{|S|}≤β for |S|≥1); sum the constant β over subsets, bound erase-∅ ⊆ univ, card = 2^k (Fintype.card_finset). This is the exact SKELETON of the generalized von Neumann inequality — the sharp version replaces β=‖b‖_∞ by the (far smaller for pseudorandom sets) Gowers U^{k−1} norm of b, which stays OPEN.

GOTCHA: applying kAPCount_norm_le to the slot fun i => if i∈S then b else 1, the bound hypothesis goal ‖(fun i => …) i x‖ ≤ (fun i => …) i has un-beta-reduced redexes on BOTH sides → rw [if_pos/if_neg] fails on the RHS lambda-application; fix with dsimp only after intro to beta-reduce, then rw fires. Also (Finset.sum_le_sum (fun S hS => ?_)).trans ?_ leaves the intermediate ∑ underdetermined → use an explicit named hterm + calc with a literal ∑_S β intermediate instead.

The k-AP count (count, nondeg, and analytic indicator Λ_k) is invariant under the full affine group x↦c·x+t (c∈(ZMod N)ˣ). Previously only the generators (translate t, dilate c, neg c=-1) were recorded separately; the single affine theorem is obtained by factoring the affine image as translate∘dilate (affine_image_eq) and chaining. This is the exact symmetry group under which nondegenerate-k-AP containment is invariant — the natural normalisation for a future density-increment argument.

Reversal (x,d)↦(x+(k-1)d,-d) is an involution that fixes the k-AP count set (image=id), for total and nondegenerate counts — a genuine reflection symmetry. It has fixed points ((k-1)d=0 ∧ 2d=0), so it does NOT force the count to be even.
